content.value_statement: Saleor storefronts can fail when pricing, variants, permissions, checkout, and channel availability are misunderstood. This skill provides practical GraphQL patterns and troubleshooting guidance for reliable implementations.
actual_capabilities: Explain Saleor nullable fields, gross pricing, discounts, and storefront visibility.
Design channel-scoped GraphQL queries, cursor pagination, filters, and code generation workflows.
Model variant selection, variant media, stock checks, and add-to-cart requirements.
Trace checkout creation, persistence, payment errors, completion, and stale checkout recovery.
Diagnose legacy and direct stock availability across channels, warehouses, and shipping zones.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not connect to a Saleor instance.
It does not generate a complete storefront application or deploy production infrastructure.
Exact fields and behavior depend on the Saleor version and generated schema.
Payment provider health and dashboard configuration require external verification.

use_cases.title: Plan a product page
use_cases.description: Map Saleor product data, variant attributes, pricing, media, and availability into a clear product page workflow.

use_cases.title: Debug checkout failures
use_cases.description: Trace checkout state, shipping methods, payment transactions, and stale identifiers to isolate completion errors.

use_cases.title: Audit channel availability
use_cases.description: Compare channel, warehouse, stock, pricing, and shipping-zone conditions when products cannot be purchased.

prompt_templates.title: Learn the Saleor model
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how Saleor products, variants, channels, prices, and checkouts relate. Use a short example for a beginner.

prompt_templates.title: Design a product query
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a channel-scoped Saleor GraphQL product query for pricing, selection attributes, media, availability, and cursor pagination. State nullable fields.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a checkout error
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this Saleor checkout error and current checkout state, identify likely causes, required checks, and the safest recovery sequence: [paste details].

prompt_templates.title: Investigate availability deeply
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Saleor channel availability problem across legacy and direct modes. Separate purchasability from shippability and produce a verification checklist: [paste configuration].

output_examples.input: Why is a product visible but not purchasable in a Saleor channel?
output: Check publication, channel listing, variant price, warehouse assignment, and stock.
In legacy mode, also check shipping-zone coverage and warehouse assignment to that zone.
In direct mode, verify shipping methods separately because visibility does not guarantee checkout success.

output_examples.input: What should a variant picker do when a selected combination does not exist?
output: Keep options visible and let the customer choose a different value.
Clear conflicting selections and resolve the selection against a specific variant.
Disable add to cart until every required selection attribute is resolved.

output_examples.input: How should a storefront handle a failed payment attempt?
output: Read the live checkout totals and transaction events.
Check for authorization failures, stale transactions, and changed shipping totals.
Use a fresh checkout when the existing checkout is invalid or accumulated failed transactions.

best_practices: Pass the channel argument on product and availability queries.
Use live authenticated checkout data for payment amounts and completion decisions.
Treat nullable fields deliberately and distinguish purchasability from shippability.
anti_patterns: Do not add a product to checkout without resolving a specific variant ID.
Do not use staff tokens or cache user-specific checkout responses.
Do not assume product availability guarantees shipping or successful checkout.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Saleor GraphQL data, permissions, products, variants, checkout, channels, stock, and API investigation.

faq.question: Does it support every frontend framework?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is framework-agnostic and applies to Next.js, Remix, Nuxt, or custom storefronts.

faq.question: Why is the channel argument important?
faq.answer: Saleor uses channels for pricing, publication, and availability. Omitting the channel can produce incomplete storefront data.

faq.question: What is the difference between variant attribute types?
faq.answer: Selection attributes identify a variant and drive pickers. Non-selection attributes describe a variant and remain display-only.

faq.question: Can available products still fail at checkout?
faq.answer: Yes. In direct availability mode, shipping zones and methods can still prevent checkout for a destination.

faq.question: Does this skill access my Saleor store?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance. Your application and credentials are required to query or change Saleor data.
